makemeahanzi.definition: to touch; to meet with; to collide, to bump into

characterDeckComponents.note: 石 (rock) — 碰 originally described one hard object, like a stone, striking another, giving 'to bump, to collide.'
並 (bìng) is only distantly related in sound to pèng — both use a bilabial initial (b/p), but the rhyme and tone have drifted apart.

etymology.hint: Two eyes shut 林 at night 夕

characterDeckComponents.note: 林 here depicts eyes shut in sleep, not its usual meaning 'forest.'
夕 (evening, night) — sleeping at night is when dreams occur, giving 梦 its meaning 'dream.'

makemeahanzi.definition: to boil, to roll, to turn

characterDeckComponents.note: 氵 (water) shows this relates to liquid, as in something boiling or rolling in water.
衮 (gǔn) gives the exact sound of 滚.

makemeahanzi.definition: to support; to respect; to put on, to wear; surname
son, child; seed, egg; fruit; small thing

etymology.hint: A child in a wrap, with outstretched arms but bundled legs

characterDeckComponents.note: A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

makemeahanzi.definition: to conceal, to hide; to hoard, to store

characterDeckComponents.note: 艹 (grass) — 藏 relates to hiding something among vegetation.
臧 (zāng) gives a rhyme close to cáng, sharing a similar initial.
广 (a building/shelter) — 底 relates to the base or bottom, as of a structure
氐 (dǐ) gives the sound — 底 is also pronounced dǐ, an exact match
忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.

makemeahanzi.definition: to change, to replace, to substitute for

etymology.hint: One man 夫 replacing another; 日 provides the pronunciation

characterDeckComponents.note: 夫 (man) is shown twice, side by side, one man standing in for another.
日 sits below, together giving 替 its meaning 'to replace, to substitute.'
面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'
A simplified pictograph of a bird's wings spread in flight — the source of 飞's meaning 'to fly.'
气 (simplified from 氣) depicts rising wisps or vapor, like breath or steam drifting upward — a simple picture of air or gas.
冫 (water/ice) — 冲 relates to liquid, as in pouring or rinsing with water
中 (zhōng) gives a sound close to 冲's reading chōng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

meanings: leg (of an animal or an object)

characterDeckComponents.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — 脚 refers to the foot, a part of the body
却 (què) gives a sound distantly related to 脚's reading jiǎo, having drifted apart over time

makemeahanzi.definition: to damage, to ruin; to defame, to slander

etymology.hint: A man using a tool 殳 to strike 工 a clay vessel 臼

characterDeckComponents.note: 臼 pictures a clay mortar or vessel.
殳 (a tool, held in a hand) strikes it, giving 毁 its meaning 'to destroy, to smash.'

etymology.hint: A man 大 wrapped in a long 镸 cloth

characterDeckComponents.note: 大 (big, a person with arms and legs spread) pictures a person.
镸 (long) pictures a long piece of cloth wrapped around them, giving 套 its meaning 'cover, case.'

makemeahanzi.definition: to weep, to cry, to wail

etymology.hint: To shed a tear from your eyes 口 over a person 犬

characterDeckComponents.note: 口 (mouth), shown twice here, standing for eyes streaming with tears.
犬 (here a stand-in for a person, not literally 'dog') — a person crying, together giving 哭 its meaning 'to weep, to cry.'

meanings: to draw (a line) (variant of 劃|划[hua4])

etymology.hint: A painting on an easel; compare 畫, which includes the brush

characterDeckComponents.note: 画 depicts a picture set within a frame — the traditional form 畫 additionally showed a hand holding a brush above it.
疒 (sickness) — relates directly to 病's meaning 'illness, disease, to be sick.'
丙 (bǐng) gives a sound hint — 病 is pronounced bìng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
纟 (thread) — relates directly to 线's meaning 'line, thread, wire.'
戋 (jiān) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from xiàn.

etymology.hint: A person 儿 carrying a torch 火

characterDeckComponents.note: 儿 (a person) — shown carrying a torch overhead, the source of 光's meaning 'light, brightness.'
火 (fire) — the torch's flame, the thing giving off the light.
礻 (an altar, related to ritual/spirits) — 神 relates to gods and spirits.
申 (shēn) gives a hint of the sound — 神 is pronounced shén, a connection that has shifted over time.

makemeahanzi.definition: to conduct, to manage, to run

characterDeckComponents.note: 扌 (hand) — 操 relates to controlling or handling something.
喿 (zào) gives a sound distantly related to cāo, having drifted apart over time.
辶 (to walk) — 道 relates to a path or road one walks along.
首 (shǒu) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer resembles dào, a reminder that sound components can drift after thousands of years of pronunciation change.

makemeahanzi.definition: to check, to control, to push, to restrain

characterDeckComponents.note: 扌 (hand) — 按 relates to pressing something with the hand
安 (ān) gives a sound close to 按's reading àn, differing only in tone

etymology.hint: To swaddle 勹 a baby 巳; 勹 also provides the pronunciation

characterDeckComponents.note: 勹 (an enclosing shape) — wrapping around.
巳 (a baby) — swaddled inside, the image of wrapping something up giving 包 its meaning 'to wrap; bag, package.'

etymology.hint: Flesh ⺼ used to walk 退; 退 also provides the pronunciation

characterDeckComponents.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — part of the body.
退 (to step back, retreat) — used to move and walk, together giving 腿 its meaning 'leg.'

etymology.hint: A nose; in China, people refer to themselves by pointing to their noses

characterDeckComponents.note: A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'

meanings: (before or after number + measure word) exactly

makemeahanzi.definition: neat, orderly, whole; to repair, to mend

characterDeckComponents.note: 敕 (an order, discipline) — relates to 整's meaning 'orderly, whole, to arrange.'
正 (zhèng) gives a sound hint — 整 is pronounced zhěng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

makemeahanzi.definition: to know, to perceive, to comprehend

characterDeckComponents.note: 口 (mouth) — 知 relates to speaking what one knows.
矢 (shǐ) gives a hint of the sound — 知 is pronounced zhī, a connection that has faded over time.

makemeahanzi.definition: bank note; ticket; vote; a slip of paper

etymology.hint: Flames 覀 over an altar 示, referring to a Chinese tradition of burning fake money as an offering

characterDeckComponents.note: 覀 here depicts rising flames.
示 (altar) — burning paper offerings over an altar, a traditional practice, gave 票 its meaning of a paper note, later 'ticket, banknote.'

meanings: classifier for sets, series, groups of people, batteries

makemeahanzi.definition: to form, to assemble; section, department

characterDeckComponents.note: 纟 (thread) — 组 originally meant 'to weave, arrange,' extended to 'group, to organize.'
且 (qiě) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from zǔ.

makemeahanzi.definition: to shine, to reflect, to illuminate

characterDeckComponents.note: 灬 (fire) — relates to 照's meaning 'to shine, illuminate; photograph.'
昭 (zhāo) gives a sound hint — 照 is pronounced zhào, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

makemeahanzi.definition: to connect; to deliver, to exchange; to intersect; to mix

characterDeckComponents.note: Depicts a person standing with legs crossed — the crossing shape gave 交 its meaning 'to intersect, exchange, hand over.'

meanings: to move (sth relatively heavy or bulky)

makemeahanzi.definition: to move, to remove, to shift, to transfer

characterDeckComponents.note: Hand — moving things is done by hand.
Gives the sound bān, matching the character's reading.
木 (wood) — buildings were traditionally framed with wood.
娄 (lóu) gives the sound — an exact match with 楼.

meanings: classifier for games: match, set, round etc

etymology.hint: A place where measures 尺 are discussed 口

characterDeckComponents.note: 尺 (a ruler/measure) — represents rules or measures being set.
口 (mouth) — measures being discussed aloud in one place gave 局 its meaning 'bureau, office, situation.'
目 (eye) — 眼 refers directly to the eye itself.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound hint — 眼 is pronounced yǎn; the rhyme has drifted apart over the centuries.

makemeahanzi.definition: fire, flame; to burn; anger, rage

characterDeckComponents.note: A pictograph of rising flames — the source of 火's meaning 'fire.'
犭 (dog, used broadly for animals) shows 猫 names an animal.
苗 (miáo) gives a sound close to māo, sharing the initial consonant.

etymology.hint: A card squeezed between 上 and 下

characterDeckComponents.note: 上 (top) — the upper edge pressing down
卜 — the lower edge, with a card squeezed between the two

makemeahanzi.definition: to bathe, to rinse, to wash

characterDeckComponents.note: 氵 (water) — 洗 describes cleaning something with water.
先 (xiān) shares the initial x- with xǐ, though the rhyme has drifted.

makemeahanzi.definition: muddy, confused; to mix, to blend; to mingle

characterDeckComponents.note: 氵 (water) — 混 originally described muddy, mixed water.
昆 (kūn) gives a sound distantly related to hùn, having drifted apart over time.

makemeahanzi.definition: to suspend, to put up, to hang; suspense

characterDeckComponents.note: 扌 (hand) — 挂 describes hanging something up using the hand.
圭 (guī) gives a sound close to guà, sharing the initial g-.

meanings: to get on (a horse etc) by swinging one leg over

makemeahanzi.definition: to cheat, to defraud, to swindle

characterDeckComponents.note: 马 (horse) — 骗 originally described swinging up onto a horse, later extended figuratively to 'to trick, to swindle.'
扁 (biǎn) shares the rhyme -ian with piàn, and both use a bilabial initial (b/p) — only voicing and tone differ.
木 (wood) — 案 originally referred to a wooden table or desk
安 (ān) gives a sound close to 案's reading àn, differing only in tone
木 (tree) — relates directly to 根's meaning 'root (of a plant or tree).'
艮 (gèn) gives a sound hint — 根 is pronounced gēn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
